summary: Independently verified ETAPA 4 / PAS 3.5 HARDENING on /app/v2 (python/pytest, local-only). Ran the 5 target hardening files single-process (-n 0): 185 passed + 2 skipped (Windows-only DPAPI/msvcrt). Added 9 extra independent tester checks in test_tester_extra_hardening.py (all passing) covering: durable cloud UID identity + idempotent atomic promote, release-ordering rules, IdentityConflict rolls back all rows and leaves witness untouched, identities scoped per cemetery_uid and reused on second bootstrap, deterministic batching under 5 random shuffles of local_snapshot, SourceDrift on altered uid_map in bootstrap_state/<id>.sqlite, PERMISSIONS['bootstrap']=={OWNER} and PERMISSIONS['rebuild']=={OWNER,REBUILD}, Admin/REBUILD/stranger/other-tenant-owner denied all staging functions (PermissionDenied or ScopeError), stale session refuses put_batch and does NOT delete rows/batches, and zero live DB writes after full transfer. Full regression suite (/app/v2/backend `pytest -q`): 405 passed / 3 failed / 154 skipped in 210s. The 3 failures are the known LEGACY ones (test_etapa1_audit::test_route_inventory_uses_only_clear_prefixes and 2 in test_etapa9b_cloud_config needing backend/.env + .env.example absent from the clone). No regressions, no deviations from expected numbers.
critical_code_review_comments: cimitir_cloud_staging._session raises ScopeError (not PermissionDenied) for other-tenant/stranger access even if cp._require passes for same-tenant case; this is intentional (information-leak hardening) but worth documenting so callers catch both exception types.
promote_transfer idempotency verified: second call returns {promoted: True, already: True, row_count: N}; witness table cloud_identity_promotions is the single source of truth. Good design.
release_local_state correctly refuses in both pre-completion and pre-promotion states (TransferBlocked).

Transfer._batches re-canonicalizes snap on every call and verifies against meta['batch_digests'] from plan time -> drift detection is robust against both source row-order changes and uid_map tampering (SourceDrift). Confirmed over 5 random shuffle seeds.

Identity scope: cloud_entity_identity has UNIQUE partial indexes on (cemetery_uid, entity_type, local_ref) WHERE status='active' and (cemetery_uid, entity_type, cloud_uid) WHERE status='active' -> correctly enforces one active cloud_uid per entity per cemetery and prevents cross-cemetery leakage.
No code was modified under /app/v2/shared/ as instructed.

success_rate.backend: 100% of target hardening tests (185/185 non-skipped) + 9/9 extra tester tests; 405/408 full suite (3 pre-existing legacy failures, unchanged)

seed_data_creation: none (uses in-fixture tmp dirs and LocalControlPlane)

Full suite `pytest -q` takes ~3.5min, expect 405/3/154 baseline. The 3 legacy failures live in test_etapa1_audit.py and test_etapa9b_cloud_config.py and are environmental (missing backend/.env* files in this clone).
rca of the issue: No new issues found. All PAS 3.5 hardening properties (durable identity, atomic promote, deterministic batching, process-kill resume, stale metadata, bootstrap vs rebuild permissions, zero live writes, cross-tenant isolation) verified both via existing suite and 9 independent tester-authored checks.
